title: The organ grinder at dances
summary: Clarifying how organ grinders worked, how long they were hired, and that they were all they had instead of a band.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: How big was that organ grinder that they grinded to say in comparison to a piano?

Was it big as an upright? It's high like that. It was on a stand. A stand on a big square like that. And it had a hand. A stand on a stand. And that's where he'd grind them. Not as big as a piano. No. Oh no, he used to push it. It had a handle on it like this. And it was high. Three feet high. Yeah, it was a man who would push it, you know. Did he play more than one tune? Oh yeah, we used to pay him. We'd hire him for so many hours. I don't know what we paid him, but we'd hire him for so many hours. And he could change the tune. He could just change the tune one after the other. I don't know how he'd done it. That's one thing I often wanted to find out, but I never did. Someday I will. Often wanted to know how he could change the tune, but I never did go ask him. How about when was that? That was when I was around 18 or 19 years old.
There was a famous guy called Nicodemus was an organ grinder here. I have a little write-up on him somewhere.
You don't see them no more.

All you see now is the organ grinder with the monkey, the little organ with the monkey. How about this one? How about this one? How about this one? How about this one? How about this one? All right, let's see, we were talking about organ grinders. I said they do have one at Cobb's, at the People grind, or a hand organ.

Well, maybe that's what I'm talking about, because they had a hand. But it used to stand, have a stand in the middle. Although it wouldn't have to have a stand, you could put it on a table or a bench or something to stand it up or a prop, however they'd fix it.
Did they have anything else to come to your house or around your house at that time for dances?

That's all I knew we ever had was the organ grinders. We wanted to hire a band, but the banjos have a lot of violin and things like that and more violin and they have cornet. But now they have more trombones and things than they used to have.
